students.name: Alastair McCullough
students.quote: Doctoral Student Graduate Teaching Assistant Student, Kellogg College E: alastair.mccullough@cs.ox.ac.uk Wolfson Building, Parks Road, Oxford OX1 3QD Themes: Human Centred Computing Interests I specialise in research, review, and design of data strategies and architectures for very large and complex organisations and in leading realisation of them. These include enterprise information and data architectures, governances, strategies, and business architectures such as target operating models. They fit in the main within the broad domains of software engineering and security (data governance). At Oxford, my doctoral research focuses on regulatory data and information governance for enterprises in the evolving contexts of big data (volume, variety, velocity, veracity, and value) and Artificial or Augmented Intelligence. Experience in the Field Commercial and other enterprises for whom I’ve designed solutions and led delivery of architectures, strategies, governances, and operating models include English Heritage, Aviva, TalkTalk, Shell, Telefonica, IBM, IAG, WPP, BBC, IKEA, E.ON, PMI, LV=, Vodafone, Lloyds Banking Group, Barclays Bank, Sony Network Entertainment Europe, Thames Water, Ford of Europe, the UK Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA), the UK Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC for NHS), the UK Government, and AstraZeneca. For the majority of these I've worked at Board (C-Suite) and senior and executive management levels. For most of these, I've either led or been a key designer and presenter of pre-sales technical solutions, project and resource design, commercial bids, financial and contract design. Engagement contracts have been valued at between around $80K and over $1Bn per organisation. Biography Alastair McCullough has designed and delivered enterprise information architecture solutions across an over thirty-year career, spanning Oracle database technologies initially, business intelligence solutions, cloud data platform design, and specialising in leading data strategy, governance and regulation design and innovation. He has founded or been a director of six start-up companies in the UK since 1989, and has over thirty years' experience as a director. The most successful start-up, a new software company subsidiary based in Oxford, generated annual turnover in excess of £2M within 24 months. Alastair's clients have included a wide range of commercial and government organisations, usually enterprises with over £1Bn annual turnover, and both civil and defence departments within the UK Government. At IBM, Alastair founded and led the Data and Analytics Competence Strategy (DACS) group in IBM's BAO Practice; the Data Strategy, Governance and Modelling consulting group in IBM's UK Data Services Practice; and the Cloud Data Modellers’ Guild in IBM Consulting in 2021. For a UK Government agency, Alastair led the £4M IMPALA Business Intelligence programme for three years. At Thames Water, Alastair served as interim Head of Data and Information Architecture, designing their £29.3M Enterprise Data Strategy for the Water industry's next regulatory period in 2017. At AstraZeneca, Alastair served as a director and global Head of Enterprise Information Architecture, leading a team of 45 information architects, data analysts and modellers and a £6.1M annual budget and department spanning India, Sweden, the UK and US until July 2023. Alastair has been elected a Fellow of the British Computer Society, a Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology, a Fellow of the Institute of Directors, and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. He is a Chartered Engineer, Charted IT Professional, and a Chartered Management Consultant. Alastair read for his BA in Business at what is now London Metropolitan University, and for his MSc in Business Systems Analysis and Design at City, University of London, where his thesis focused on Fourth Generation Synergetic Database Management System Environments, and at which he was subsequently a Visiting Lecturer. Teaching Alastair has written and taught a wide variety of classes and courses for academic and commercial groups and audiences for many years, both focused seminar-style lectures, shorter sessions, multi-day intensive classes, and presentations for large and global international cohorts. Themes covered have included: Data Strategy Design and Delivery Data and Information Governance - Introductory through to advanced levels The EU General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR, and its application to technology and regulatory governance IBM Information Technology Architecture, Methodology, and Management Technical Project and Programme Management Data Modelling Oracle technologies and languages, including SQL, Advanced SQL, PL/SQL, Oracle Forms, Oracle Reports, NoetixViews and Oracle Applications Executive presentation techniques. Alastair has been a Visiting Lecturer at City, University of London, and an IBM Visiting Lecturer at Portsmouth University, Warwick University, and at Imperial College. At Imperial, he led an IBM team including IT Architects, Distinguished Engineers and consulting professionals teaching an annual intensive short course focusing on IBM IT Architecture methods for classes of 30 to 50 second-year BSc Electrical and Electronic Engineering students, for nine years up until 2019. In May 2025, in conjunction with COGS, the Computer Science Graduate Society, and the Oxford Careers Service, Alastair delivered the Computer Science, Mathematics, and Statistics Careers Keynote at the Oxford University Mathematical Institute. His presentation is available here. Today, Alastair teaches on the Oxford Computer Science department's Professional Master's Programme for the MSc in Software Engineering, Building Information Governance module: Professional MSc BIG Module. Recognition 2022 Award: Chartered Engineer (Enterprise Information Architecture), The Engineering Council (CEng) 2020 Elected Fellow of The Royal Society for the Encouragement of Arts, Manufactures and Commerce (FRSA) Elected Fellow of The British Computer Society (FBCS) - Chartered Fellow Award: Chartered Management Consultant, The Chartered Management Institute (MCMI ChMC) Award: IBM Certified Expert Consultant, IBM Corporation 2019 Elected Fellow of The Institute of Directors (FIoD) Award: IBM Certified Expert IT Architect, IBM Corporation Award: Master Certified Architect, Solution Architecture, The Open Group Award: Chartered Information Technology Professional, The British Computer Society (CITP) 2018 Elected Fellow of The Institution of Engineering and Technology (FIET) 2016 Award: Certified Architect, Solution Architecture, The Open Group Award: IBM Certified Experienced IT Architect, IBM Corporation. Alastair is a Professional Member of the Association for Computing Machinery, the ACM. Alastair has served as a member of the IET's Digital Policy Panel until 2024 and is today a member of the Community of Policy Experts, focusing on the work of the IET's Digital Policy Centre. He was one of the first hundred Chartered Management Consultants to be awarded ChMC by the Chartered Management Institute in the UK. Alastair was recognised as a Chartered Engineer (CEng) by the Engineering Council in 2022 based on his professional work in leading and defining enterprise information architectures cross-industry for over 17 years. External Projects Digitalization Strategy - Alastair served as IBM Technical Leader, Data Themes, for six years with the Cambridge Service Alliance, a collaboration between industry, the Institute for Manufacturing (IfM), Judge Business School, and Cambridge University. Most recently (2024 - 2026), Alastair has been collaborating with specialist researchers based across Stockholm University, Linköping University, Universidad Autónoma de Madrid, Durham University, and Surrey University, together developing new thinking on Digitalization Strategy in Service Ecosystems, arising from a September 2024 forum held in Cambridge University, sponsored by the Cambridge Service Alliance. students.name: Alastair McCullough
students.quote: Doctoral Student Graduate Teaching Assistant Student, Kellogg College E: alastair.mccullough@cs.ox.ac.uk Wolfson Building, Parks Road, Oxford OX1 3QD Themes: Human Centred Computing Interests I specialise in research, review, and design of data strategies and architectures for very large and complex organisations and in leading realisation of them. These include enterprise information and data architectures, governances, strategies, and business architectures such as target operating models. They fit in the main within the broad domains of software engineering and security (data governance). At Oxford, my doctoral research focuses on regulatory data and information governance for enterprises in the evolving contexts of big data (volume, variety, velocity, veracity, and value) and Artificial or Augmented Intelligence. Experience in the Field Commercial and other enterprises for whom I’ve designed solutions and led delivery of architectures, strategies, governances, and operating models include English Heritage, Aviva, TalkTalk, Shell, Telefonica, IBM, IAG, WPP, BBC, IKEA, E.ON, PMI, LV=, Vodafone, Lloyds Banking Group, Barclays Bank, Sony Network Entertainment Europe, Thames Water, Ford of Europe, the UK Driver and Vehicle Licensing Agency (DVLA), the UK Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC for NHS), the UK Government, and AstraZeneca. For the majority of these I've worked at Board (C-Suite) and senior and executive management levels. For most of these, I've either led or been a key designer and presenter of pre-sales technical solutions, project and resource design, commercial bids, financial and contract design. Engagement contracts have been valued at between around $80K and over $1Bn per organisation. Biography Alastair McCullough has designed and delivered enterprise information architecture solutions across an over thirty-year career, spanning Oracle database technologies initially, business intelligence solutions, cloud data platform design, and specialising in leading data strategy, governance and regulation design and innovation. He has founded or been a director of six start-up companies in the UK since 1989, and has over thirty years' experience as a director. The most successful start-up, a new software company subsidiary based in Oxford, generated annual turnover in excess of £2M within 24 months. Alastair's clients have included a wide range of commercial and government organisations, usually enterprises with over £1Bn annual turnover, and both civil and defence departments within the UK Government. At IBM, Alastair founded and led the Data and Analytics Competence Strategy (DACS) group in IBM's BAO Practice; the Data Strategy, Governance and Modelling consulting group in IBM's UK Data Services Practice; and the Cloud Data Modellers’ Guild in IBM Consulting in 2021. For a UK Government agency, Alastair led the £4M IMPALA Business Intelligence programme for three years. At Thames Water, Alastair served as interim Head of Data and Information Architecture, designing their £29.3M Enterprise Data Strategy for the Water industry's next regulatory period in 2017. At AstraZeneca, Alastair served as a director and global Head of Enterprise Information Architecture, leading a team of 45 information architects, data analysts and modellers and a £6.1M annual budget and department spanning India, Sweden, the UK and US until July 2023. Alastair has been elected a Fellow of the British Computer Society, a Fellow of the Institution of Engineering and Technology, a Fellow of the Institute of Directors, and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts. He is a Chartered Engineer, Charted IT Professional, and a Chartered Management Consultant. Alastair read for his BA in Business at what is now London Metropolitan University, and for his MSc in Business Systems Analysis and Design at City, University of London, where his thesis focused on Fourth Generation Synergetic Database Management System Environments, and at which he was subsequently a Visiting Lecturer. Teaching Alastair has written and taught a wide variety of classes and courses for academic and commercial groups and audiences for many years, both focused seminar-style lectures, shorter sessions, multi-day intensive classes, and presentations for large and global international cohorts. Themes covered have included: Data Strategy Design and Delivery Data and Information Governance - Introductory through to advanced levels The EU General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR, and its application to technology and regulatory governance IBM Information Technology Architecture, Methodology, and Management Technical Project and Programme Management Data Modelling Oracle technologies and languages, including SQL, Advanced SQL, PL/SQL, Oracle Forms, Oracle Reports, NoetixViews and Oracle Applications Executive presentation techniques. Alastair has been a Visiting Lecturer at City, University of London, and an IBM Visiting Lecturer at Portsmouth University, Warwick University, and at Imperial College. At Imperial, he led an IBM team including IT Architects, Distinguished Engineers and consulting professionals teaching an annual intensive short course focusing on IBM IT Architecture methods for classes of 30 to 50 second-year BSc Electrical and Electronic Engineering students, for nine years up until 2019. In May 2025, in conjunction with COGS, the Computer Science Graduate Society, and the Oxford Careers Service, Alastair delivered the Computer Science, Mathematics, and Statistics Careers Keynote at the Oxford University Mathematical Institute. His presentation is available here. Today, Alastair teaches on the Oxford Computer Science department's Professional Master's Programme for the MSc in Software Engineering, Building Information Governance module: Professional MSc BIG Module. Alastair has served as a member of the IET's Digital Policy Panel until 2024 and is today a member of the Community of Policy Experts, focusing on the work of the IET's Digital Policy Centre. He was one of the first hundred Chartered Management Consultants to be awarded ChMC by the Chartered Management Institute in the UK. Alastair was recognised as a Chartered Engineer (CEng) by the Engineering Council in 2022 based on his professional work in leading and defining enterprise information architectures cross-industry for over 17 years. Her research interests broadly span LLM post-training and evaluation; AI safety and scalable oversight; the reliability and factuality of AI systems; and foundational questions in AI ethics and the philosophy of AI, including AI alignment. She also studies large-scale AI deployments and their wider societal and economic implications, taking an end-to-end perspective on aligning, evaluating, and responsibly deploying advanced AI systems in high-stakes settings. Alongside her doctoral studies, Nimisha serves as an International Consultant at The World Bank in Washington, D.C., USA, where her work focuses on factuality, AI evaluation, and assessing the real-world impacts of multi-agent AI systems deployed at global scale. Previously, she was a Student Researcher at Google DeepMind in London focusing on multimodal co-creation and steering generative AI systems. Prior to beginning her doctoral studies at Oxford, Nimisha worked full-time for two years as a Research Fellow at Microsoft Research India. students.quote: Doctoral Student Student, Balliol College E: jiachen.qian@cs.ox.ac.uk Department of Computer Science, Robert Hooke Building Directions Postal Address Themes: Security Automated Verification Interests My research interests include formal verification, automated mathematical reasoning, and automated theorem proving, which together offer a rich intersection of theoretical exploration and practical application. These fields are essential for the verification of hardware and software systems. Beyond their practical importance, a more ambitious goal is to explore the extent to which machines can aid mathematicians in conducting complex reasoning tasks, verifying proofs, and even autonomously generating novel proofs! Biography I completed my MSc in Mathematics and Foundations of Computer Science at the University of Oxford. Prior to that, I received my undergraduate degree in Mathematics at the University of Sheffield, where I primarily focused on pure mathematics. A previous internship in industry introduced me to symbolic reasoning and automated theorem provers, including Isabelle and Lean, which sparked a shift in my research interests toward theoretical computer science.
